name: Loading Button
summary: A loading button is a button that shows it is working after you press it. A spinner is a picture, so on its own it tells a screen reader nothing: the state has to go in `aria-busy` and in a live region beside the button. The button also has to keep its focus and keep its name while it works.
demoNote: Press any button here and the readouts record what a screen reader was handed. Every example under Common mistakes is live.

contract.useWhen: A button that is working, saying so to someone who cannot see the spinner.
keyboard: native: the stop survives going busy, because aria-disabled is used and never disabled
native: aria-disabled blocks the handler, so a second press does nothing
states: busy — aria-busy=true and aria-disabled=true, set only while pending
failureModes: no aria-busy and no region, so the only cue is an animation
the disabled attribute while pending, which drops focus and announces nothing
the label swapped to a progress word, renaming the control mid-press
the spinner as the only cue, gone under forced colors and reduced motion
